subject: Bounded owned Option/Result record execution and memory-budget reclamation
claim: Nine source-generated minor-39 programs execute successfully on Windows and Debian with deterministic, identical WVB bytes. Three owned-record shapes each complete 128 allocation/observation/release cycles; a refusal case releases 128 child budgets and an oversized capacity returns the exact unaddressable failure. Eight copied-payload mutations reject at both complete-verifier and runner boundaries, and two invalid budget-ownership sources reject at emitter WIR validation.

source.value: Worktree based on e08415d0cdfa87443b038e6bf155c6a8da638d69 with exact changed source identities below. Authenticated native predecessor products constructed the updated emitter, which constructed the updated runner. No bootstrap or installed identity was promoted.

runs.target: Nine publication/execution scenarios, eight copy mutations at two boundaries, and two invalid budget ownership sources
The same nine programs, copy mutations and budget rejection cases; all nine WVB digests match Windows
Existing ten-case borrowed-value runner regression selection
Existing ten-case borrowed-value runner regression selection

limitations: The selected payloads are Option and either Result side containing a generic record that owns an i32 Vector, plus a Copy-record control. Observation reads the record marker through an immutable borrow, not Vector contents. No maintained owned-resource consumer was migrated.

The successful loops each split 8192 bytes 128 times under a 98304-byte/64-child root. The refusal loop splits 16 bytes, requests a 40-byte Vector, and checks Budget-exhausted with exact requested/available values. Capacity 2048 checks Target-unaddressable with requested=16392 and available=0. These are bounded host-profile results, not arbitrary resource or payload support.

The runtime change admits existing budget parameter/local/variant shapes and reserved Vector construction for exact minor 39. Construction and Memory.Split remain Main-only. Direct Vector extraction, borrowed Vector helper observations, exclusive borrowing, Take, mapping, unsafe operations, task execution, native lowering and installed promotion are not newly supported by this checkpoint.

The compiler fix addresses temporary tables by declared ID instead of block traversal order. The failing loop visits an exit producing temporary 31 before a body producing temporary 10. Bounds, consumption and cross-block checks remain. Three additional local WIR mutations (undefined ID, duplicate ID, consumed cross-block budget) rejected on both hosts; these ad-hoc diagnostics supplement the retained source rejection controls rather than adding a verifier entry point.

The emitter source build took 178383 ms and the final runner source build took 238307 ms on Windows. Both packages consumed Windows-constructed WVB/images. Native Debian execution and byte agreement do not establish independent Debian reconstruction. Peak memory was not measured; no performance-improvement claim is made.

Explicit reusable compiler, admission and complete-verifier products were supplied. The plan-only conservative routing proposed 2550 seconds across nine owners; unrelated reconstruction, editor, backend, OS and whole-repository qualification were not executed. Existing runtime regressions were rerun only after their runner dependency changed. No broader gate is claimed.
The earlier publication-only checkpoint remains a historical record. Its unsupported owned executions are superseded only for the exact runtime scope recorded here.
